title: SI base units of kinetic energy
subject: physics
stem:
The kinetic energy \(E_{k}\) of an object of mass \(m\) moving at speed \(v\) is given by
\[
E_{k}=\tfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}
\]
Determine the SI base units of kinetic energy.

steps.title: Unit of mass
steps.prompt: In your working, what is the SI base unit of \(m\)?
steps.explanation: Mass is a base quantity measured in kilograms.

steps.title: Units of v²
steps.prompt: What are the SI base units of \(v^{2}\)?

steps.title: Final answer
steps.prompt: What are the SI base units of \(E_{k}\)?
steps.explanation: \(\tfrac12\) has no units, so \(\mathrm{kg}\times\mathrm{m^{2}\,s^{-2}}\). The joule is a derived unit.

title: Homogeneity: period of a simple pendulum
subject: physics
stem:
The period \(T\) of a simple pendulum of length \(l\) is given by
\[
T=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}
\]
where \(g\) is the acceleration of free fall.

Use SI base units to show whether this equation is homogeneous.

steps.title: Units of l/g
steps.prompt: In your working, what are the SI base units of \(\dfrac{l}{g}\)?

steps.title: Units of the right-hand side
steps.prompt: What are the SI base units of \(2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}\)?

steps.title: Final answer
steps.prompt: What is your conclusion?
options: Not homogeneous: the right-hand side has units of s²
Homogeneous: both sides have units of s
Homogeneous: both sides have units of s⁻¹
steps.explanation: \(T\) is a time, in \(\mathrm{s}\), and the right-hand side is also in \(\mathrm{s}\), so the equation is homogeneous.

title: SI base units of a drag constant
subject: physics
stem:
At high speed, the drag force \(F\) on a car is given by
\[
F=kv^{2}
\]
where \(v\) is the speed of the car and \(k\) is a constant.

Determine the SI base units of \(k\).

steps.title: Rearranged equation
steps.prompt: What expression for \(k\) did you use?

steps.title: Units of F
steps.prompt: What are the SI base units of \(F\)?

steps.title: Final answer
steps.prompt: What are the SI base units of \(k\)?

title: SI base units of resistivity
subject: physics
stem:
The resistivity \(\rho\) of the material of a wire is given by
\[
\rho=\frac{RA}{L}
\]
where \(R\) is the resistance of the wire, \(A\) is its cross-sectional area and \(L\) is its length.

Determine the SI base units of \(\rho\).

steps.title: Units of potential difference
steps.prompt: In your working, what are the SI base units of potential difference?

steps.title: Units of R
steps.prompt: What are the SI base units of resistance \(R\)?

steps.title: Units of A/L
steps.prompt: What are the SI base units of \(\dfrac{A}{L}\)?

steps.title: Final answer
steps.prompt: What are the SI base units of \(\rho\)?

title: Prefixes: area and volume of a wire
subject: physics
stem:
A copper wire has a diameter of \(0.48\,\mathrm{mm}\) and a length of \(2.5\,\mathrm{m}\).

Calculate, in standard form,

(a) the cross-sectional area of the wire in \(\mathrm{m^{2}}\),

(b) the volume of the wire in \(\mathrm{m^{3}}\).

steps.title: Radius in metres
steps.prompt: What radius, in metres, did you use?
steps.explanation: \(0.48\,\mathrm{mm}=4.8\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m}\), and the radius is half of that.

steps.title: (a) Area
steps.prompt: What is the cross-sectional area?

steps.title: (b) Volume
steps.prompt: What is the volume of the wire?

title: Uncertainty: resistance from meter readings
subject: physics
stem:
The circuit shown is used to determine the resistance \(R\) of a resistor.

The readings are:
- voltmeter: \((6.0\pm0.1)\,\mathrm{V}\)
- ammeter: \((0.50\pm0.02)\,\mathrm{A}\)

(a) Calculate \(R\).

(b) Determine the absolute uncertainty in \(R\), and write \(R\) with its uncertainty.

steps.title: (a) Resistance
steps.prompt: What value of \(R\) did you calculate?

steps.title: Percentage uncertainty in R
steps.prompt: What percentage uncertainty in \(R\) did you find?

steps.title: (b) Final answer
steps.prompt: How should \(R\) be written with its absolute uncertainty?

title: Uncertainty: area of a rectangular sheet
subject: physics
stem:
The length and width of a rectangular sheet of metal are measured as:
- length \(=(25.0\pm0.2)\,\mathrm{cm}\)
- width \(=(12.0\pm0.1)\,\mathrm{cm}\)

Calculate the area of the sheet, and give it with its absolute uncertainty.

steps.title: Area
steps.prompt: What area did you calculate?

steps.title: Percentage uncertainty
steps.prompt: What percentage uncertainty in the area did you find?

steps.title: Final answer
steps.prompt: How should the area be written with its absolute uncertainty?
steps.explanation: \(1.6\%\) of \(300\) is \(4.9\approx5\,\mathrm{cm^{2}}\). Absolute uncertainties are not simply added for a product.

title: Uncertainty: kinetic energy of a trolley
subject: physics
stem:
A trolley of mass \((0.250\pm0.005)\,\mathrm{kg}\) moves at a speed of \((4.0\pm0.2)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

(a) Calculate the kinetic energy of the trolley.

(b) Determine the absolute uncertainty in the kinetic energy.

steps.title: (a) Kinetic energy
steps.prompt: What kinetic energy did you calculate?

steps.title: Percentage uncertainty in v²
steps.prompt: What percentage uncertainty did \(v^{2}\) contribute?

steps.title: Total percentage uncertainty
steps.prompt: What total percentage uncertainty in the kinetic energy did you find?

steps.title: (b) Absolute uncertainty
steps.prompt: What is the absolute uncertainty in the kinetic energy?

title: Uncertainty: specific heat capacity from a temperature rise
subject: physics
stem:
A heater supplies \((5400\pm50)\,\mathrm{J}\) of energy to \((0.100\pm0.001)\,\mathrm{kg}\) of water. The thermometer readings at the start and end are shown. Each reading has an uncertainty of \(\pm0.5\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\).

The specific heat capacity \(c\) of water is given by
\[
c=\frac{E}{m\,\Delta T}
\]
(a) Determine the temperature rise \(\Delta T\) with its uncertainty.

(b) Calculate \(c\).

(c) Determine the absolute uncertainty in \(c\).

steps.title: (a) Temperature rise
steps.prompt: What temperature rise, with its uncertainty, did you find?
steps.explanation: \(35.0-21.5=13.5\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\). For a difference, the absolute uncertainties add: \(0.5+0.5=1.0\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\).

steps.title: (b) Specific heat capacity
steps.prompt: What value of \(c\) did you calculate?

steps.title: Percentage uncertainty in c
steps.prompt: What percentage uncertainty in \(c\) did you find?

steps.title: (c) Absolute uncertainty
steps.prompt: What is the absolute uncertainty in \(c\)?

title: Uncertainty: density of a stone by displacement
subject: physics
stem:
A stone of mass \((45.0\pm0.1)\,\mathrm{g}\) is lowered into a measuring cylinder containing water. The water level before and after is shown. Each reading of the cylinder has an uncertainty of \(\pm1\,\mathrm{cm^{3}}\).

(a) Determine the volume of the stone.

(b) Calculate the density of the stone, and give it with its absolute uncertainty.

steps.title: (a) Volume
steps.prompt: What volume of the stone did you find?
steps.explanation: \(58-40=18\,\mathrm{cm^{3}}\). Two readings are subtracted, so the uncertainties add: \(\pm2\,\mathrm{cm^{3}}\).

steps.title: Density
steps.prompt: What value of the density did you calculate?

steps.title: Percentage uncertainty
steps.prompt: What percentage uncertainty in the density did you find?

steps.title: (b) Final answer
steps.prompt: How should the density be written with its absolute uncertainty?

title: Vectors: aircraft in a crosswind
subject: physics
stem:
An aircraft is heading due north with a speed of \(120\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) relative to the air. A wind blows towards the east at \(50\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), as shown.

Determine

(a) the resultant speed of the aircraft,

(b) the angle between the resultant velocity and due north.

steps.title: (a) Resultant speed
steps.prompt: What resultant speed did you find?

steps.title: Trig ratio
steps.prompt: Which expression did you use for the angle \(\theta\) from north?
steps.explanation: Measured from north, the side opposite \(\theta\) is the wind, \(50\), and the adjacent side is \(120\).

steps.title: (b) Angle
steps.prompt: What angle from due north did you find?

title: Vectors: components of weight on a slope
subject: physics
stem:
A block of weight \(50\,\mathrm{N}\) rests on a slope inclined at \(25^{\circ}\) to the horizontal, as shown.

Calculate the component of the weight

(a) parallel to the slope,

(b) perpendicular to the slope.

steps.title: Angle used
steps.prompt: In your working, what is the angle between the weight and the line perpendicular to the slope?
steps.explanation: The angle between the weight and the normal to the slope equals the angle of the slope, \(25^{\circ}\).

steps.title: (a) Parallel component
steps.prompt: What component parallel to the slope did you find?

steps.title: (b) Perpendicular component
steps.prompt: What component perpendicular to the slope did you find?

title: Vectors: resultant displacement of a hiker
subject: physics
stem:
A hiker walks \(3.0\,\mathrm{km}\) due east, then \(5.0\,\mathrm{km}\) in a direction \(30^{\circ}\) north of east, as shown.

Determine

(a) the magnitude of the hiker's resultant displacement,

(b) the direction of the resultant displacement, as an angle north of east.

steps.title: East component
steps.prompt: What total eastward component did you find?

steps.title: North component
steps.prompt: What total northward component did you find?
steps.explanation: Only the second walk has a northward part: \(5.0\sin30^{\circ}=2.50\,\mathrm{km}\).

steps.title: (a) Magnitude
steps.prompt: What magnitude of displacement did you find?

steps.title: (b) Direction
steps.prompt: What direction did you find?

title: Vectors: two tugs pulling a ship
subject: physics
stem:
Two tugboats pull a ship using horizontal cables. One cable has a tension of \(3000\,\mathrm{N}\) and the other a tension of \(2000\,\mathrm{N}\). The angle between the cables is \(40^{\circ}\), as shown.

Determine

(a) the magnitude of the resultant force on the ship from the two cables,

(b) the angle between the resultant force and the \(3000\,\mathrm{N}\) cable.

steps.title: Component along the 3000 N cable
steps.prompt: Taking the \(3000\,\mathrm{N}\) cable as your reference direction, what total component along it did you find?

steps.title: Component perpendicular to it
steps.prompt: What total component perpendicular to the \(3000\,\mathrm{N}\) cable did you find?
steps.explanation: Only the \(2000\,\mathrm{N}\) force has a perpendicular part: \(2000\sin40^{\circ}=1290\,\mathrm{N}\).

steps.title: (a) Resultant
steps.prompt: What magnitude of resultant force did you find?

steps.title: (b) Angle
steps.prompt: What angle between the resultant and the \(3000\,\mathrm{N}\) cable did you find?
steps.explanation: \(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1290}{4530}\right)=15.8^{\circ}\). It is not half of \(40^{\circ}\), because the forces are unequal.

title: Kinematics: ball kicked at an angle
subject: physics
stem:
A ball is kicked from level ground with a velocity of \(18\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) at \(35^{\circ}\) above the horizontal, as shown. Air resistance is negligible. Take \(g=9.81\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).

Calculate

(a) the maximum height reached by the ball,

(b) the horizontal distance from where the ball is kicked to where it lands.

steps.title: Vertical component
steps.prompt: What initial vertical velocity did you use?

steps.title: Horizontal component
steps.prompt: What horizontal velocity did you use?

steps.title: (a) Maximum height
steps.prompt: What maximum height did you find?
steps.explanation: At the top the vertical velocity is zero: \(h=\dfrac{10.3^{2}}{2\times9.81}=5.43\,\mathrm{m}\).

steps.title: Time of flight
steps.prompt: What total time in the air did you find?
steps.explanation: Time to the top is \(\dfrac{10.3}{9.81}=1.05\,\mathrm{s}\); the flight is twice that, \(2.10\,\mathrm{s}\).

steps.title: (b) Horizontal distance
steps.prompt: What horizontal distance did you find?

stem:

Calculate

(a) the time taken for the police car to catch up with the car,

(b) the distance travelled by the police car in this time,

(c) the speed of the police car when it catches up.

steps.title: Equation for the police car
steps.prompt: What expression for the displacement of the police car after time \(t\) did you use?

steps.title: (a) Time
steps.prompt: What time did you find?

steps.title: (b) Distance

steps.title: (c) Speed
steps.prompt: What speed of the police car did you find?
steps.explanation: \(v=at=2.5\times12=30\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). It is double the car's speed, as expected when starting from rest.

title: Kinematics: v–t graph of a lift
subject: physics
stem:
The velocity–time graph shows the motion of a lift as it moves upwards between two floors of a building.

Use the graph to determine

(a) the deceleration of the lift as it comes to rest,

(b) the distance between the two floors,

(c) the average speed of the lift.

steps.title: (a) Deceleration
steps.prompt: What deceleration did you find?
steps.explanation: The gradient of the last section: \(\dfrac{3.0}{11-8}=1.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).

steps.title: Distance while accelerating
steps.prompt: What distance did the lift move in the first \(2.0\,\mathrm{s}\)?

steps.title: (b) Total distance
steps.prompt: What distance between the floors did you find?

steps.title: (c) Average speed
steps.prompt: What average speed did you find?

title: Kinematics: stone thrown down from a bridge
subject: physics
stem:
A stone is thrown vertically downwards from a bridge with a speed of \(5.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). It hits the water \(3.0\,\mathrm{s}\) later. Air resistance is negligible. Take \(g=9.81\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).

Calculate

(a) the height of the bridge above the water,

(b) the speed of the stone as it hits the water.

steps.title: Values of u and a
steps.prompt: Taking downwards as positive, what values of \(u\) and \(a\) did you use?
steps.explanation: The stone is thrown downwards, so \(u=+5.0\), and gravity acts downwards, so \(a=+9.81\).

steps.title: (a) Height
steps.prompt: What height did you find?

steps.title: (b) Speed
steps.prompt: What speed at the water did you find?
